references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a), 28(1), read 2026-10-07: a deduction from salary only for the employee’s own absence from the place they are required to work. A shutdown or temporary closure by the employer is not the employee’s absence: the day counts as attended and the monthly salary is paid whole.

Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a), 28(1), read 2026-10-07: a deduction from salary only for the employee’s own absence from the place they are required to work. A lockout keeps the employee from work by the employer’s act: attended, salary whole.

Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a), 28(1) (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/EmA1968?ProvIds=pr27-,pr28-), read 2026-10-07: a deduction from salary only for the employee’s own absence from the place they are required to work. Workplace Safety and Health Act 2006 s.21 (https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/WSHA2006?ProvIds=pr21-): a stop-work order ceases the work, not the contract; for a work-pass holder the declared fixed salary stays payable (EFM (Work Passes) Regulations 2012 Fourth Schedule).

name: Natural disaster or force majeure closure

references.title: Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a), 28(1), read 2026-10-07: a deduction from salary only for the employee’s own absence from the place they are required to work. A workplace closed by a natural disaster or other force majeure is not the employee’s absence; Singapore has no statutory shutdown allowance. An employee who cannot reach an open workplace is absent (NO_PAY_LEAVE).

Employment Act 1968 ss.27(1)(a), 28(1), read 2026-10-07: a deduction from salary only for the employee’s own absence from the place they are required to work. A striking employee is absent from work: the day is not attended and the employer may deduct for it under s.28(2) through a NO_PAY_LEAVE entry; there is no suspension pay.
